tokenRules.message: Hex color hardcoded. Use semantic tokens (var(--primary), var(--bg-surface), var(--text-default), ...).
RGB/HSL hardcoded. Use semantic tokens via var(--*).
Tailwind palette color. Use semantic webkit tokens (var(--primary), var(--text-default), var(--bg-surface), ...).
Raw Tailwind text size. Use a generated typography class (text-heading-md, text-body-sm, text-button-lg, ...).
Legacy/external color utility. Use semantic webkit tokens (var(--text-default), var(--bg-surface), ...).

bounce.useWhen: Playful attention bounce (scroll-down hints); use sparingly.

brand-marquee.useWhen: A strip of logos looping forever (client trust strips, framework strips). Apply to a track holding its row exactly twice, the duplicate aria-hidden, and set animation-duration ON THE ELEMENT from the mark count so every strip on a site moves at one speed rather than one duration — a var in this shorthand would resolve at :root and never see it. Pause it on hover and focus-within so a linked mark can be reached.

content-enter.useWhen: Content settling INSIDE a page that is already on screen — a loading window resolving, a filtered list swapping, a step changing. Never on first paint of a page whose own entrance is already running (use it after that entrance, or after a wire). Stagger a follower with --content-enter-delay.

fade-in.useWhen: Content or backdrop appearing in place (no directional origin).

fade-out.useWhen: Content or backdrop leaving in place (pair of fade-in).

flow-dash.useWhen: Flowing connection along an SVG connector stroke in a node-based / network diagram. Set a stroke-dasharray whose cycle divides 24 (e.g. 4 4) so the loop is seamless.

highlight-fade.useWhen: Row/item briefly highlighted after an update (recently changed).

page-enter.useWhen: A page arriving on a route change — on the CONTENT ZONE only, never the shell. The chrome is the same before and after, and sliding it announces a reload that did not happen. Key it on the route path so a component serving several paths still replays it. Nothing inside the page may animate on mount at the same time: the two run in lockstep and read as one element travelling on a diagonal.

ping.useWhen: One-off attention ring radiating from a small element (notification dot).

popup-scale-in.useWhen: Anchored overlays opening (dropdown, popover, tooltip, menu); set --popup-origin.

progress-indeterminate-short.useWhen: Indeterminate linear progress bar (secondary short sweep).

pulse.useWhen: Skeleton/placeholder opacity pulse while content loads.

shimmer.useWhen: Skeleton shimmer sweep while content loads.

slide-down.useWhen: Vertical disclosure expanding (accordion panel, expandable row).

slide-in-end.useWhen: End-anchored panel entering (settings/detail drawer); flips with the reading direction.

slide-in-start.useWhen: Start-anchored panel entering (sidebar, navigation drawer); flips with the reading direction. Wrap the v-if region in a Vue Transition with enter-active-class.

slide-out-start.useWhen: Start-anchored panel leaving (pair of slide-in-start; use as leave-active-class).

texture-wave-a.useWhen: One of the two crossing bands of a pixelate texture, travelling left. Set --texture-wave-shift on the element to one period of its banding measured along X, and overhang the element by that much on the side it travels toward, or the field uncovers mid-cycle.

texture-wave-b.useWhen: The counter-travelling band of that pair (pair of texture-wave-a; same --texture-wave-shift contract, opposite direction).

heading level of a title the component renders
where a link opens (target, as on button and link)

props.name: title

props.name: variant

props.name: confirmationPhrase

props.name: denyLabel

props.name: loading

props.doc: Visual variant applied to both joined segments.

props.doc: Size token; affects height, padding, and typography.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables both segments and prevents the menu from opening.

props.doc: Shows a spinner on the primary button and takes the disabled status: both segments are disabled and the menu cannot open while it resolves.

props.doc: When true, selecting a menu action updates the primary button's label and icon to mirror that action and marks it as selected in the menu. Opt-in; the mirrored action is also reported as the primary `click`'s second argument, so the consumer decides what each segment does.

props.name: selectedKey
props.doc: Two-way value (`v-model:selectedKey`).

events.name: item-click
events.notes: Fired when a menu action is selected. `event` is the pointer/keyboard event that activated the option; `item` is the matched `items` entry. The menu cannot open while `disabled` or `loading`, so it never fires in those states.

props.doc: column definitions (`{ id?, accessorKey?, header?, label?, sortable?, grow?, principal?, frozen?, width?, minWidth?, align?, type?, resizable?, hideable?, orderable? }`; `width` (px) sets a fixed pixel column (also needed when a frozen column precedes another frozen column on the same edge, so sticky offsets can be summed); **`minWidth`** (px) sets a **floor** instead: the table measures the column's own content — its header, including the sort affordance, and every rendered body cell — and pins the column to the larger of the two, as **one** width applied to the header and every body cell (a per-cell `min-width` would let each row size to its own content and drift the header away from the body). It is for a column whose content is a chip or a short token: a fixed `width` there is a bet in both directions — too generous and it reserves space the rest of the row needs, too tight and the chip inside it truncates. The measured width tracks the **rendered page**, so a column can change width when paging or sorting brings longer content into view; `width` wins when both are set, and a user resize wins over both. a `grow` column without `width` keeps a shared fixed basis so the header and body stay aligned and the cell never wraps. A column with no `grow` defaults to weight `2` for the **principal** column and `1` for the rest, so the columns fill the available space proportionally. The principal column is the one flagged `principal: true`, or — when none is flagged — the first non-action column. A `type: 'action'` column is automatically pinned to the trailing (right) edge — staying reachable while the rest scrolls horizontally — and is never resizable. **`resizable: true`** opts a column into a live mouse/touch drag-to-resize handle on its header (native pointer events; the `@tanstack/vue-table` exception covers sorting/pagination/selection/visibility, not sizing). On the first drag of any divider every flexible column freezes at its current rendered width; from then on dragging changes **only that column** and the table grows (horizontal scroll) — the others are untouched. The drag floor is the column's own content width (header label + visible body cells), so a column never shrinks past its content. Frozen and action columns ignore `resizable`. **`label`** names the column in `CollectionPreferences` when `header` is not a string; **`hideable: false`** lists the column locked in `CollectionPreferences`; **`orderable: true`** opts the column into `columnOrder`.

Sorting and filtering keep each child under its parent; selection is per row (selecting a parent does not select its children). `reorderable` is ignored in tree mode.

props.name: align
props.doc: Alignment along the trigger edge.

props.name: sideOffset
props.doc: Pixel gap between the trigger and the panel.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Prevents the trigger from opening the panel and applies disabled tokens.

props.name: size
props.doc: Panel width preset mapped to container tokens: `'small'` (`var(--container-xs)`), `'medium'` (`var(--container-sm)`), `'large'` (`var(--container-md)`). When omitted, the panel sizes fluidly between `var(--container-3xs)` and `var(--container-xs)`. Same name as the size preset of `Dialog`, `Drawer` and `ConfirmDialog`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Initial open state when uncontrolled (`v-model:open` unbound).

props.name: dismissible
props.doc: Light-dismiss: when `true`, the panel closes on outside-click and `Esc`. Set `false` to keep it open until the trigger or `PopoverClose` closes it.

props.name: open
props.doc: Two-way value (`v-model:open`).

slots.name: default
slots.notes: Place `<Popover.Trigger>` followed by `<Popover.Content>`.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name; when set the spinner renders role status with this name, otherwise it stays aria-hidden. Size and color come through `class`.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale of everything below the provider; picks the catalog from `catalogs` (English is built in) and the `Intl` formats. Empty follows the device locale, `en-US` on the server and until mount.

props.name: catalogs
props.doc: Extra catalogs keyed by locale tag, imported from `@aziontech/webkit/locales/<tag>` (`{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }`); a locale with no catalog falls back to English.

props.name: messages
props.doc: Partial catalog deep-merged over the built-in one, keyed by component group (`{ pagination: { next: 'Seguinte' } }`).

props.name: dir
props.doc: Text direction of the subtree; `auto` derives it from the locale (`ar`, `he`, `fa`, `ur` are right-to-left).

props.name: now
props.doc: Reference time for every relative time below the provider (`TableCellTime`, `useLocale().formatRelativeTime`, the day groups of `ConversationHistory`, the relative ranges of `DateRangePicker` when their own `now` is unset); unset reads the real clock, ticking each minute.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: IANA time zone every `Timestamp` below the provider shows its local time in, and every `DateRangePicker` with no `v-model:time-zone` formats in (`America/New_York`, `UTC`), for an app-wide time zone picker; empty reads the browser's zone.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The app, or the part of it that shares this locale.

account/account-hierarchy.name: AccountHierarchy
account/account-hierarchy.title: Blocks/Account/AccountHierarchy
account/account-hierarchy.summary: The account hierarchy: organizations, groups and workspaces in one `DataTable` with tree rows (`get-sub-rows`, `v-model:open-keys`, a treegrid with the row-focus keyboard map) and row selection. A `PageHeader` with Create Workspace, a search `Input` over name, ID, type and labels that keeps the ancestors of each match (a small `EmptyState` with Clear search when nothing matches), the paginated tree, an action row with Create Group, the bulk Move, Labels and Delete that act on the selection, Refresh and Hide details, and a details panel with Permissions (role bindings of the one selected resource as `KeyValueList`) and Labels tabs. Move picks a new parent in a `Dialog` (never the resource itself or anything inside it); Labels adds and removes labels on every selected resource; Delete counts what is inside in a `ConfirmDialog` and keeps it in Resources pending deletion for 30 days; each ends in a toast, Move and Delete with Undo. A page body for ConsoleLayout, rendered in its default slot.
account/account-hierarchy.guidelinesSummary: Where an account admin arranges the account's hierarchy. Workspaces sit under groups, groups under organizations, and a role binding set on a parent applies to everything under it, so where a workspace lives decides who can reach it. The page shows the whole hierarchy as one tree table, lets the admin select across levels and act on the selection (move, label, delete), and shows the role bindings and labels of the one resource selected. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

account/activity-history.name: ActivityHistory
account/activity-history.title: Blocks/Account/ActivityHistory
account/activity-history.summary: The account's audit log: a `PageHeader` with Documentation over one controls row (`PropertyFilter` on event, category, user and IP address; a `DateRangePicker` for the period, last 30 days by default; Refresh, Download CSV and `CollectionPreferences`) and a `DataTable` of events, newest first: Event, Category as a `Tag`, User, IP address with a `CopyButton`, and Date as `TableCellTime`. One `useCollection` holds filter, sort, page and saved preferences; the period narrows the items before it. An empty period offers a longer one, filters that match nothing offer Clear filters, and a failed load is a danger `Alert` with Retry. A page body for ConsoleLayout, rendered in its default slot.
account/activity-history.guidelinesSummary: The account's audit log. An admin or a security reviewer answers "who did this, from where, and when": a token that was revoked, a role that changed, a sign-in that failed, a plan that was upgraded. They narrow the log by period, category, person and address, read the newest events first, copy an IP address into another tool, and export what they found. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

account/billing.name: Billing
account/billing.title: Blocks/Account/Billing
account/billing.summary: The Billing page of the account settings: a `PageHeader` with the last update, Refresh and Documentation over `PageTabs` (Bills, Payment methods). Bills puts a Subscription plan `Card` (plan with a Current plan `Tag`, Change plan, and `KeyValueList` for plan start, next charge date and value as `CurrencyAmount`, and the default card with its `PaymentBrand`) beside an Upgrade to Enterprise `Card`, then Invoices on one `useCollection`: a controls row (`PropertyFilter`, Refresh, Download CSV, `CollectionPreferences`) over a `DataTable` with No., Invoice ID, Plan, Cycle, Seats, Billing date, Amount, Payment method, Status as `TableCellStatus` and a download `IconButton` per invoice. Payment methods shows Payment information as `KeyValueList` (billing email, auto-renewal as `StatusIndicator`, address, tax ID) with Update, and a `DataTable` of cards (holder with a Default `Tag`, brand and last four, expiry, `TableCellActions` with Set as default and Remove behind a `ConfirmDialog`). Outcomes go through `toast`. A page body for ConsoleLayout, rendered in its default slot.
account/billing.guidelinesSummary: What the account pays, what it paid and which card it is charged to. An admin checks the current plan and the next charge, moves to another plan, finds and downloads an invoice, and keeps the cards on file current: which one is the default, which ones to remove. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

account/deployment-settings.name: DeploymentSettings
account/deployment-settings.title: Blocks/Account/DeploymentSettings
account/deployment-settings.summary: The account's Build and deployment settings. A `PageHeader` with Documentation and the primary Create Deployment Setting, a closable info `Alert` that explains what a Deployment Setting is, then three `SettingsSection`s. New service defaults: a flush `Card` of `SettingsRow`s in an `Item.List` with a binding policy `Select`, a deployment policy `Select` and an Apply to existing `Switch`, saved through a `SaveBar` that appears only with unsaved changes (Discard, Save). All services: a collapsible `Accordion` whose trigger counts the services and tags how many share a setting; inside, a search `Input` (a small `EmptyState` with Clear search when nothing matches) and, ten services per page with `Pagination`, one row per environment with environment and policy `Tag`s, a `Select` that rebinds it to a matching Deployment Setting (inactive ones disabled), and Linked automatically and Shared `Tag`s; a rebind ends in a toast that warns when the setting now reaches several services. Deployment Settings: the table-view controls row (`PropertyFilter`, Refresh and Download CSV as `IconButton`s with a `Tooltip`, `CollectionPreferences`) over a `DataTable` on one `useCollection` (Name with a System `Tag` for Default, Services with a Shared `Tag` and the service names on a `Tooltip`, Type hidden by default, Binding policy, Deployment policy, `TableCellStatus`, `TableCellTime` for Last modified, `TableCellActions` with Edit, Clone and Delete behind a `ConfirmDialog`). Create and Edit open a large `Drawer` form (Name, Description, Active `Switch`, binding and deployment policy `RadioGroup`s). Loading draws `Skeleton`s; no services draws an `EmptyState`. Its toasts go through `toast` into the app's one toast region. A page body for ConsoleLayout, rendered in its default slot.
account/deployment-settings.guidelinesSummary: How every deploy in the account routes. A Deployment Setting holds a binding policy (whether a version locks the resource IDs it shipped with) and a deployment policy (one live version, or a URL per version); every environment of every service publishes with exactly one, linked automatically to a setting that matches its own deployment policy. On this page an admin sets the defaults the next service starts with, sees which environment publishes with which setting, points two environments at the same setting so one deploy reaches both, and manages the settings themselves. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

account/personal-tokens.guidelinesSummary: The Personal tokens page of the account settings. A person creates a token for a script, a CI job or the CLI, copies its secret the one time it is shown, sees which tokens are still alive and when each expires or was last used, and revokes one that leaked or is no longer needed. The secret never comes back: the list shows only the name, status and dates, and a lost secret means a new token. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

account/team-permissions.guidelinesSummary: Who can do what in the account. An admin keeps one team per role (Administrators, Developers, Security, Finance), sees what each grants and how many people it covers, and creates or edits a team by ticking View and Edit per resource in one matrix. People get permissions only through teams; nothing is granted per person, so the list of teams is the whole access model. The list is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`. Create Team and Edit Team are full pages in the creation frame instead (building block I).

account/users.guidelinesSummary: Who can sign in to the account, with which role and through which teams. An admin invites a teammate by email, chooses their teams, sees who has not accepted yet, resends or cancels an invitation, changes a person's role, moves a person between teams and removes people who left. The role decides what a person can do on the account itself (Admin manages people, teams and billing; Developer and Viewer do not); resource permissions come only from teams (`account/team-permissions`), so this page never grants a single permission to a person. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

ai/ai-action-approval.name: AiActionApproval
ai/ai-action-approval.title: Blocks/Ai/AiActionApproval
ai/ai-action-approval.summary: A user-authorized action inside a generative AI conversation: the reader asks the assistant to deploy, the assistant records the read-only call it made (`ToolCall`), explains in `StreamingResponse` and proposes the deployment as an `ToolApproval` card whose title names the command in code, whose body shows the exact command in a `CodeBlock`, and whose Deny and Deploy buttons decide. Approving turns the card into Approved and adds a running `ToolCall` that completes, followed by a `ChatMessage` that reports what changed with Copy (`CopyButton`); denying or letting the request expire records the outcome on the card and the assistant says nothing ran. The `PromptInput` shows Stop while the approved action runs. Built from `Conversation`, `ChatMessage`, `ToolCall`, `StreamingResponse`, `ToolApproval`, `CodeBlock`, `CopyButton` and `PromptInput`. A page body for ConsoleLayout that fills its content region.
ai/ai-action-approval.guidelinesSummary: The moment an assistant needs permission. The reader asked for something that changes their account — a deployment, a purge, a deletion — and the assistant stops before doing it: it says what it found, shows exactly what will run, and waits for Approve or Deny. The decision stays in the thread as text, and the assistant reports what happened next, so the conversation is also the record of what ran and who allowed it. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: it fills the layout's content region (`grow basis-0 min-h-0`, never `h-dvh`), so only the log scrolls, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

auth/sign-in.name: SignIn
auth/sign-in.title: Blocks/Auth/SignIn
auth/sign-in.summary: The signed-out screens of a platform app, frame included: a full-height page with the signed-out `AppHeader` (the product mark and a Documentation button) over a centred column that holds one `Card` and the prompt and terms under it. It serves /login, /signup and /signup/verify, and the signed-in hand-offs that share the frame: the OAuth authorize screen (scopes, Allow / Deny) and device or CLI authorization (compare the code, Confirm). An app that signs in with an Azion personal token instead of an account uses the PersonalToken variant (`token-sign-in.vue`): one masked `PasswordInput` for the token, a link to where tokens are created, a Remember for this tab option, and a `sign-in` event that hands the token to the app, which answers with `loading` and `error`. The Google and GitHub buttons lead the card, over an “or” `Separator`. The card opens on a `PageHeader` and signs in in two steps: email, then password. Each field is a `Field` whose `Field.Label` sits over an `Input`, or over a `PasswordInput` with `PasswordRequirements`; a `FieldError` (email) or `Field.Error` (password) appears only after the primary action. While a request is in flight the primary `Button` shows its loading state and the step's fieldset is disabled. The rest is `Button`, `IconButton` in a `Tooltip`, a `Tag` and an `Alert`. Errors follow one rule: auth never toasts. Each error story is the primary flow with one endpoint response: the same two-step card on its password step, and the outcome in the same small `Alert` under the heading. What changes is the severity and what it carries: nothing after a 401, because the fields under it are the recovery; Retry when nobody can fix it (503, 500, timeout); the Sign in and reset-your-password links when the address is already registered (409). In-page actions (Forgot your password?, Resend email, Set a new password) are `Button` with `variant="link"`, never an anchor to `#`. Built from `PageHeader`, `AppHeader`, `Tag`, `Card`, `Alert`, `Input`, `Field`, `PasswordInput`, `PasswordRequirements`, `FieldError` and `Button`. The card column slides in from the inline start with a fade on mount (`starting:` styles, `duration-slow-01`, `ease-expressive-entrance`, none under reduced motion), and the card height eases between steps. A full page routed outside ConsoleLayout.
auth/sign-in.guidelinesSummary: The signed-out screens of a platform app: sign in, sign up, reset password and check your inbox, frame included. The user has one job here, to get into their account, and one object on the page to do it with: a single card under the signed-out bar. Every step of the flow (`email`, `password`, `reset`, `sent`, `new-password`) swaps the contents of that card in place, and every answer the server gives, success included, lands in one `Alert` inside it. Auth never toasts. It is a full page with its own focused header: the app routes it outside `ConsoleLayout`, never into the layout's default slot.

Add Domain opens from under Domains on the resource’s Settings tab, from a domain row menu to edit it, and from Add Environment in the resource environment menu. The Environment select lists every environment, says when choosing one connects it to the resource, and ends in a Create Environment option. Choosing Bring my own domain drops the free-domain addon and reveals the Certificate select, preselecting a certificate that already covers the address. Built from `SettingsSection`, `Drawer` and its parts, `PanelHeader`, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `Field` (with `InputGroup`), `RadioGroup` (`variant="card"`), `Field` with `Field.Description` and `Field.Error` around `Select`, `NumberInput`, `Input`, `Textarea`, `Link`, `Alert` and `Button`. CreateEnvironment is the Create Environment drawer, on its own or stacked above Add Domain; FunctionInstance adds or edits a function instance whose arguments are a `SchemaForm` with a Fields or JSON (`CodeEditor`) `ToggleGroup`. The variants add `PageHeader`, `SettingsRow`, `Card`, `Item`, `Switch`, `Textarea`, `SchemaForm`, `CodeEditor` and `ToggleGroup`.
create/create-drawer.guidelinesSummary: The right-side drawer that adds or edits something that only exists inside another resource: a domain, a DNS record, an environment, a variable, a rule. The user is working on the resource behind it and must keep it in view, so the form slides over the page instead of replacing it. They fill a few sections, press the one commit button and land back where they were, with the new item in the list. The drawer opens over a console page: ItemRows and NestedDrawer draw that page as a page body for `ConsoleLayout` (the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`).

create/create-hub.name: CreateHub

create/create-wizard.name: CreateWizard
create/create-wizard.title: Blocks/Create/CreateWizard
create/create-wizard.summary: The page a first-level resource is created on one step at a time, built on the `Wizard` component: the creation header, a page heading, then the Wizard with its step rail on the start side (completed steps reachable, later ones locked), the current step's heading and fields, and its footer with Cancel, Previous and Next, Next turning into the create action on the last step. Next validates the step it leaves and stays put with the message under the field when it fails; a Review step shows the create's loading state and confirms it in a toast. Every create asks first where the resource runs: a chooser lists the hosts it can bind to, six at a time with a search, and tags the ones missing a module the resource needs; choosing one with that module off inserts a step that offers to turn it on. Each resource brings its own field steps, plus an Advanced step when the endpoint has optional settings. CreateAndDeploy is the same frame for a resource that is bound to another and deployed in one act (a service that serves a project on a domain): Project, then Domain and deployment, ending on Create and deploy. Built from `Wizard`, `PageHeader`, `SettingsRow`, `AppHeader`, `Input`, `Tag`, `Card`, `Alert`, `Field` with `Switch`, `RadioGroup` (`variant="card"`), `Item`, `Textarea`, `FieldError` and `Button`.
create/create-wizard.guidelinesSummary: The page a first-level resource is created on one step at a time. It is the `Wizard` component in a creation page: the user first says where the resource runs, then answers each step's fields in order, and only reaches the create action on the last step. The Wizard's rail shows how far they are and lets them return to any step already passed; if the host they chose lacks a module the resource needs, a step is inserted that offers to turn it on, so nothing is created that would silently never be read. The same frame creates a resource that must be bound and deployed in one act (CreateAndDeploy).

create/deploy-drawer.name: DeployDrawer
create/deploy-drawer.title: Blocks/Create/DeployDrawer
create/deploy-drawer.summary: The drawer a platform deploys from, opened by the outlined Deploy button on a service or a project. Needs attention is what makes it more than a report: every entry ends in one action. This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard.name: ServiceMonitoringDashboard
dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard.title: Blocks/Dashboard/ServiceMonitoringDashboard
dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard.summary: The service monitoring dashboard pattern: a PageHeader with the one window ToggleGroup, status tiles with sparklines, multi-series charts and an alert rail. One StatTile per service carries its p95 latency, the change against the previous period and a sparkline, with a StatusIndicator naming its state in words. Below, Latency (p50, p95, p99) and Error rate (Status 4xx, Status 5xx) sit in ChartCards as multi-series line Charts read over that window, while an Open alerts rail holds the right edge: a fixed-width column that scrolls on its own, independent of the tiles and charts, listing each alert as a whole-row Item link to the alert in an Item.Group with a severity Tag. Under the xl breakpoint the rail folds below the charts and the page scrolls as one. Its root carries data-layout-fill and scrolls itself: from xl the charts and the alerts rail scroll on their own; below xl the page scrolls as one.
dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard.guidelinesSummary: The page an on-call engineer keeps open: is every service up, how fast is it answering, how many requests fail, and which alerts are open right now. One tile per service states its p95 latency and its state in words; latency percentiles and error rates sit in two charts read over one window; the open alerts live in a rail on the right that scrolls on its own, so the alerts stay in view while the reader studies a chart. This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`. Its root carries `data-layout-fill`, so the layout's `main` stops scrolling and the root fills it: from `xl` the charts column and the alerts rail scroll on their own; below `xl` the root itself scrolls, so the page still scrolls as one (`h-dvh` only sizes a standalone preview).

detail/deployment-logs.name: DeploymentLogs
detail/deployment-logs.title: Blocks/Detail/DeploymentLogs
detail/deployment-logs.summary: The deploy logs of a build or deploy run with known steps, wherever it is shown: `LogViewer.Steps` lists the pipeline as an Accordion of steps, each with its status glyph and the status in words for assistive technology, its title and sentence, its time and its own LogViewer, or every line as one continuous LogViewer in the Complete view, with a flush Progress on the bottom edge while it runs. On its own its toolbar row reports the step count and the step in flight, or the outcome Tag, the time and the Phased or Complete switch once it has settled. In a create flow (InCreateFlow) it sits in a Card titled Deployment that opens on a cloning splash (a source tile, a marching dashed connector and a large destination tile) with a Cloning StatusIndicator, and once a run fails the card header carries the view switch and its footer Edit and Redeploy. On a deployment page (DeploymentDetail, DeploymentError, DeploymentQueued) it is the Deployment logs card under a status banner and the Deployment details card. Built from `LogViewer` (`LogViewer.Steps`), `Tag`, `Card`, `StatusIndicator`, `ToggleGroup` and `Button`; the deployment pages add `Alert`, `Accordion`, `Avatar`, `CopyButton`, `DropdownMenu`, `IconButton`, `EmptyState` and `Tooltip`. The deployment pages are page bodies for ConsoleLayout.
detail/deployment-logs.guidelinesSummary: The user started a deployment and wants to know where it is, whether it went live and, when it did not, exactly which step failed and why. This block shows the pipeline as ordered steps, each with its status, its one-line outcome, its time and its own log output, so the user can follow the run as it streams, then read the full output once it settles. It is the one deploy-log block: the same steps sit in the deploy card of a create flow and on a deployment's own page.

detail/dns-zone-detail.name: DnsZoneDetail
detail/dns-zone-detail.title: Blocks/Detail/DnsZoneDetail
detail/dns-zone-detail.summary: A DNS zone detail page, opened from its index: a full-bleed tab bar with Main settings and Records over a scrolling tab panel. Main settings is a settings form in the form column: four stacked sections (General, Configure your nameserver, DNSSEC, Status), each an anchored heading with a hint glyph over a flush `Card` of `ItemList` rows. Name and Domain Name are required `Input`s that show a required `FieldError` only after a failed save; the three nameservers and, while DNSSEC is on, the key tag, algorithm, digest type and digest are read-only code `Input`s in an `InputGroupRoot` with a transparent `CopyButton`; DNSSEC and Active are `Switch`es; editing anything raises the save bar at the bottom. Records is a small-heading list inside the tab (Documentation and Add Record actions) with the TableView controls row (`PropertyFilter` over Name, Type, Policy and Value, Refresh, Download CSV and `CollectionPreferences`, all driven by `useCollection`) and a records table paginated at 10: the value cell pins a copy button, Weight and Description stay blank when they do not apply, the row menu carries Edit and Delete, and the empty slot separates no records (Add Record, Import zone file) from no match (Clear filters). Built from `PageHeader`, `PageTabs`, `SettingsSection`, `SettingsRow`, `SaveBar`, `Tabs`, `Card`, `ItemList`, `Input`, `InputGroupRoot`, `CopyButton`, `Switch`, `FieldError`, `Button`, `PropertyFilter`, `CollectionPreferences`, `DataTable` and `EmptyState`. A page body for ConsoleLayout.
detail/dns-zone-detail.guidelinesSummary: The detail page of a resource that owns a long list of records, here a DNS zone. The user arrives from the zones index to do one of two jobs: adjust the zone itself (name, nameservers, DNSSEC, status) and save, or find, add, edit and delete the records the zone answers with. A tab bar splits the two jobs so the settings form and the records table never share a scroll. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header, the ⌘K palette and the `main`.

detail/domains-card.name: DomainsCard
detail/domains-card.title: Blocks/Detail/DomainsCard
detail/domains-card.summary: The domains card of a resource settings tab: a borderless data-driven table of the addresses the resource answers on, each with its environment as the row's one medium rounded tag, its deployment policy as text, its certificate as a verified glyph and text, and a row actions menu, over a footer that counts them and adds one. Rendered in the Domains section of a resource’s Settings tab, where an environment-less domain leaves its Environment and Policy cells empty and the count reads domain or domains. Built from `Card`, `DataTable`, `Tag`, `TableCellActions` and `Button`.
detail/domains-card.guidelinesSummary: A short list of the things one resource is attached to, shown in place inside its Settings tab. Here they are its domains: the user sees every address the resource answers on, which environment, deployment policy and certificate each one uses, and can edit, delete or add one without leaving the settings page.

detail/get-started.name: GetStarted
detail/get-started.title: Blocks/Detail/GetStarted
detail/get-started.summary: The onboarding block for a resource made from the CLI: a section heading with a toggle between the CLI and GitHub Actions paths, then three numbered step cards, each with a code block for its commands. It sits under the summary on a resource Overview tab and at the end of a create wizard, on the deploy success screen. Built from `SectionHeader`, `ToggleGroup`, `Card` and `CodeBlock`.
detail/get-started.guidelinesSummary: The first thing a user reads about a resource they created from the CLI and have not deployed yet. They need the exact commands to build and ship it, in order, for the path they work with: the CLI on their own machine or a GitHub Actions workflow. The block names the two paths, lets them pick one and walks them through three numbered steps, each with commands they can copy.

detail/invocations.name: Invocations
detail/invocations.title: Blocks/Detail/Invocations
detail/invocations.summary: The Invocation page of one function run, as a page body for ConsoleLayout: one run end to end. A `PageHeader` titled Invocation opens on the invocation summary `Card` (the function `Link`, the copyable invocation ID with its `StatusIndicator`, Replay, the Recent switcher, an outlined `Button` whose `DropdownMenu` picks another invocation, the Invocation actions menu with Open in Real-Time Events and Function settings, the Started, Completed, Duration and Location facts, and the triggering request with its outcome). Below it the Request path is a `FlowDiagram` with one node per hop (service, resource, function, origin), each with its `Tag`, its facts and the time spent there; a node's `IconButton` selects its span in the `Trace` waterfall and scrolls it into view. The `LogViewer` lists what the function printed, timed on the same clock as the trace. The Error variant opens on a run the origin timed out, with the failing span selected; Running shows a run still in progress, its spans running and the lines printed so far under a Streaming indicator. Built from `PageHeader`, `Card`, `Tooltip`, `CopyButton`, `StatusIndicator`, `Button`, `DropdownMenu`, `IconButton`, `Link`, `SectionHeader`, `FlowDiagram`, `Tag`, `Trace`, `LogViewer` and `LogViewerContent`; Replay emits `replay`, which the page reports through `toast`.
detail/invocations.guidelinesSummary: The page a user opens to understand one run of a function: did it work, how long did it take, where did the time go, and what did the code print. It reads top to bottom from the answer to the evidence: the invocation summary, the path the request travelled, the trace that measured each step, and the logs on the same clock. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the layout owns the rail, the header with the breadcrumb (Functions › the function › Invocations) and the `main`.

detail/production-checklist.name: ProductionChecklist
detail/production-checklist.title: Blocks/Detail/ProductionChecklist
detail/production-checklist.summary: A production checklist on a resource overview: a card that names the gates between the generated hostname and production, counts how many are done and lists each as a row, with an expand button (named by a `Tooltip`) and clickable rows that open the same list as a drawer where every step carries its description and its action. Once every gate is done the card collapses to its title with a Ready for production Tag. Rendered on a resource’s Overview tab. Built from `Card`, `Item`, `Tag`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `Drawer`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter` and `Button`.
detail/production-checklist.guidelinesSummary: A service that is live on its generated hostname is not yet ready for real traffic. This card tells the user what stands between the service and production (a custom domain, a security policy, custom error pages), how many of those gates are done and which one to take next. It expands into a drawer where each gate explains itself and offers its action, and it shrinks to a single line once every gate is done.

detail/resource-detail.name: ResourceDetail
detail/resource-detail.title: Blocks/Detail/ResourceDetail
detail/resource-detail.summary: The Overview tab of a resource detail page: the full-bleed tab bar, sticky while the layout scrolls, then the column that opens on the resource summary card. The resource overview follows it with Get started for a resource made from the CLI, and the same page plots its Versions tab (the versions table) and its Build tab (repository, build configuration and token bands); the service overview follows the summary with the production checklist and the deployment topology. The summary card on its own, in its resource, service and policy shapes, is the Resource, Service and Policy variants: a subject band with the primary link and the actions, a band of labelled facts, and a state band on the canvas fill. A deployment's own page (success, failure, queued) is the DeploymentLogs template and one function run is the Invocations template. The FirstDeploy variant draws the summary cards before and during the first deploy, ResourceBuildConnected the Build tab with a connected repository, and ApplicationBuild the application page with a Build tab and the project drop target. The Application variant is a whole application page with Overview, Versions, Deployments and a Topology tab built on `TopologyDiagram`, whose staged binds deploy through a `Drawer` and the Edit and Redeploy toast. The version page of a resource is the VersionDetail template and the deploy drawers opened from these pages are the DeployDrawer template (Templates/Platform/Create/DeployDrawer). The Deployments tab of a resource and of a service is the TableView controls row over a deployments table, scoped to the resource (the resource tab adds a small Deployments heading with Documentation and an outlined Deploy action); the service Settings tab is a variant of Templates/Platform/Edit/EditResource. Built from `PageHeader`, `PageTabs`, `SectionHeader`, `SettingsSection`, `SettingsRow`, `SaveBar`, `Tabs`, `DataTable`, `EmptyState`, `InputGroupRoot`, `Card`, `DropdownMenu`, `Popover`, `Accordion`, `TopologyDiagram`, `Item`, `Drawer`, `Alert`, `CodeBlock` and `ToggleGroup`; the summary card variants add `Button`, `IconButton`, `Tag`, `StatusIndicator`, `Avatar`, `CopyButton` and `Tooltip`. A page body for ConsoleLayout: the layout owns the rail, the header with the breadcrumb (a service's environment crumb is its `breadcrumbs` slot) and the main.
detail/resource-detail.guidelinesSummary: The second-level page of one resource. The user arrives from a list row or a deploy flow to answer three questions about it: where it lives and whether it is serving, what it is made of, and what to do next. The page names the resource in the breadcrumb, splits its concerns into tabs, and opens the Overview tab on one summary card of facts, followed by whatever the resource needs next: Get started for a resource made from the CLI, the production checklist and topology for a service. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header with the breadcrumb, the ⌘K palette and the `main`.

detail/sectioned-resource.name: SectionedResource
detail/sectioned-resource.title: Blocks/Detail/SectionedResource
detail/sectioned-resource.summary: A resource page whose tab holds more sibling pages than a tab row can carry: the third navigation level, and the only sanctioned home for a `SidebarMenuRoot` inside a page body. A full-bleed `PageTabs` row names the resource's sections (here a policy: Web security, Network security, Private access, Data protection, Objects, Settings, Versions); the Private access tab carries 16 sibling pages in 4 groups. From `@3xl` of the tab body the local navigation is a `SidebarMenuRoot` of groups in a fixed `--container-3xs` column, its rows `href` links with no glyphs, like rail sub-rows, and exactly one row marked current, derived from the route; below `@3xl` it folds into a medium `Select` labelled with the tab name through `Field`, its options grouped the same way. Beside it the current page is the TableView body: a small `PageHeader` with an outlined Documentation and an outlined Add action, the `PropertyFilter` controls row with Refresh, and a flush `Card` around `DataTable` driven by `useCollection`, with an `EmptyState` inside the table that tells a page with no entries (Add) apart from a filter that matches nothing (Clear filters); another tab shows an `EmptyState` linking to that tab's route. The container query sits on the tab body wrapper and the queries on its children, so the content column never drops below the page column minus the navigation column. Use it only when the rail does not already list these pages and the tab has more than 7 siblings; with 7 or fewer, use a `ToggleGroup` (the FewSiblings variant), tabs or sections of one page. A page body: render it in the default slot of ConsoleLayout, which owns the rail, the header and the main.
detail/sectioned-resource.guidelinesSummary: The page of one resource whose tab holds more sibling pages than a tab row can carry: the rules of a policy, the records of a zone, the settings of one application. The user arrives from the resource's list row or its tabs and moves between the sibling pages without leaving the resource. A console screen shows one navigation per level: the rail lists modules and first-level pages, `PageTabs` lists the resource's sections, and this block adds the third level, at most one local navigation inside the active tab. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header with the breadcrumb, the ⌘K palette and the `main`.

detail/version-detail.name: VersionDetail
detail/version-detail.title: Blocks/Detail/VersionDetail
detail/version-detail.summary: One version of a resource, opened from its Versions tab, as a page body for ConsoleLayout: the layout's last crumb is a transparent select that switches between the resource versions, each with its state Tag, or creates a new one (the page sets it with `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumb`; below md the body's own row carries it with a Back button); the root carries `data-layout-fill`, so the layout's main gives the workspace the height under the header. In the body a horizontal `Resizable` holds the version workspace, a tab bar with Settings, Source, Device Groups, Cache Settings, Functions Instances and Rules Engine carrying the state Tag and a Version actions menu, the open tab in a fading `ScrollArea`, and the version bar pinned to the bottom that names the state and holds the Save and deploy `SplitButton` on a draft or Add Version and Redeploy on a built version, and a collapsible Version history pane with the current version, its changes and the earlier built versions. The primary opens on the Settings tab; the Source, Device Groups, Cache Settings and Functions Instances variants open on their tab (a list with the controls row and an add or edit `Drawer`), Creating draws the workspace as `Skeleton` wires while a new version is copied, NotFound is the `EmptyState` for a version that does not exist, and the Rules Engine tab is the Edit/RuleBuilder template. Built from `ConfirmDialog`, `PageHeader`, `PageTabs`, `SettingsSection`, `SettingsRow`, `Select`, `Resizable`, `Tabs`, `Tag`, `DropdownMenu`, `ScrollArea`, `Card`, `Item`, `Input`, `Switch`, `SplitButton`, `Button`, `Avatar`, `Field`, `Textarea`, `DataTable`, `Drawer`, `MultiSelect`, `NumberInput`, `SchemaForm`, `CodeEditor`, `Breadcrumb` and `EmptyState`; its toasts go through `toast` into the app's one toast region (ToastPlugin, or one Toaster at the app root), never a Toaster in the page body.
detail/version-detail.guidelinesSummary: One version of a resource, opened from its Versions tab. The user is here to change a draft and ship it, or to read what a built version holds and redeploy it or branch a new version from it. The page keeps the version they are on in the breadcrumb, where they can switch to another, puts the version's settings in tabs, pins the state and the save or deploy action to the bottom, and opens the version history beside the work when they need to see what changed. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header with the breadcrumb, the ⌘K palette and the `main`. The workspace pins its own bars, so its root carries `data-layout-fill`: the layout's `main` stops scrolling, the root fills it (`h-dvh` only sizes a standalone preview) and its panes scroll.

edit/delete-dialog.name: DeleteDialog
edit/delete-dialog.title: Blocks/Edit/DeleteDialog
edit/delete-dialog.summary: The destructive confirmation a resource list uses for Delete: a warning `Alert`, a sentence naming what goes with the resource and a Help Center link, then a prompt that shows the resource name in code type with a `CopyButton` beside it and an input the user must match before Delete enables. Every resource list, a folder of files and a table of records open it from the row Delete action; the title reads Delete plus the resource kind, and a container that holds other items passes its own consequence sentence. Delete shows its loading state while the request runs (Cancel and the input are locked, the dialog cannot be dismissed), then closes with a success toast; a refused delete keeps the dialog and the typed name and swaps the warning for a danger `Alert` saying why (Error). The typed confirmation resets each time the dialog opens, so the content stays put while it closes. Built from `ConfirmDialog` (the body in its default slot, its own Cancel and Delete buttons with `loading` and `disabled`), `Alert`, `CopyButton`, `Input` and `Button`; closed by default behind a visible danger trigger. The SettingsRow variant is the settings-page delete: an outlined `Item` row opens the same `ConfirmDialog` with a labelled `Field` + `Input` in its body.
edit/delete-dialog.guidelinesSummary: The last stop before a resource is gone for good. The user chose Delete from a row menu or a settings page and now has to see what goes with the resource, take one deliberate step to prove they mean this one, and either confirm or back out. The dialog makes the irreversible action slow on purpose: Delete stays disabled until the typed name matches. SettingsRow draws the page it is opened from as a page body for `ConsoleLayout` (the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`).

edit/edit-resource.name: EditResource
edit/edit-resource.title: Blocks/Edit/EditResource
edit/edit-resource.summary: The settings page of a resource, a page body for ConsoleLayout (the layout's breadcrumb names the resource): a small Settings page heading over stacked `SettingsSection` bands in the form column, each a heading with an anchor-link button and a hint glyph over a flush `Card` of field rows. The commit band is not there at rest: on the first edit a zero-height sticky strip at the bottom of the scroll region slides up a full-bleed band with a top rule, an info glyph, the unsaved-changes label with an optional muted hint, and Discard beside Save (stacked under the label on small screens), and it leaves once Save lands or Discard restores the record. The account settings pages end with the same band. A resource with a tab bar renders it as its Settings tab; a first-level resource with no tabs renders it as its own `/<resource>/:id/settings` page. Variants cover a record changed elsewhere (warning `Alert` with Reload, overwrite confirmation), the Danger zone with a typed-name delete, and the leave guard from `useUnsavedChanges` with the dirty mark on the tab. Built from `PageHeader`, `PageTabs`, `SettingsSection`, `SettingsRow`, `SaveBar`, `Tabs`, `Card`, `Item`, `Input`, `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `Switch`, `Textarea`, `RadioGroup` choice cards (`variant="card"`), `DataTable`, `Tag`, `Tooltip`, `Alert`, `ConfirmDialog`, `CopyButton`, `FieldDescription` and `Button`, with `useUnsavedChanges`.
edit/edit-resource.guidelinesSummary: The settings page of one existing resource. The user comes here to change how the resource is named, what it runs with and whether it is active, review the change, and commit it or throw it away. Every field sits in a labeled section of the form column, and one save band appears only once something has changed, so the page reads as the resource's current state until the user edits it. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header with the resource breadcrumb, the ⌘K palette and the `main`; the save band sticks to the bottom of the layout's scrolling region.

edit/function-editor.name: FunctionEditor
edit/function-editor.title: Blocks/Edit/FunctionEditor
edit/function-editor.summary: The code editor page, a page body for ConsoleLayout (the layout's breadcrumb names the service): the Code and Settings tabs, an editor toolbar whose ToggleGroup switches between the Code document and the Arguments document, and under it either one editor filling the pane or the Arguments split, a Resizable with the collapsible schema editor on the left and the form fields on the right. Both editors are a `CodeEditor` filling its pane with zero-padded line numbers and the Monaco loader from the code-editor spec. On Settings the tab holds the General, Runtime, Execution environment and Status sections, with the unsaved-changes bar: Save shows its loading state while Discard and the fields wait, a saved change raises a success toast, and a failed save keeps the bar with a danger `Alert`. Fields reorder with Move up and Move down buttons. Its page-level parts are `PageTabs`, `SettingsSection`, `SettingsRow` and `SaveBar`.
edit/function-editor.guidelinesSummary: The editing page of a service whose behavior lives in source code. The user writes and saves the code, defines the argument form each instance of the service asks for (its fields, types and defaults), and adjusts the service's settings. The editor fills the page so the code has room, and one save bar commits code, arguments and settings together. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header with the Services breadcrumb, the ⌘K palette and the `main`. The editor pins its own panes, so its root carries `data-layout-fill`: the layout's `main` stops scrolling and the root fills it (`h-dvh` only sizes a standalone preview).

edit/rule-builder.name: RuleBuilder
edit/rule-builder.title: Blocks/Edit/RuleBuilder
edit/rule-builder.summary: A rule builder drawer, the richest form pattern: a large right-side drawer with General, Phase, Criteria, Behaviors and Status sections over a single Save in the footer. Name shows its required state only after Save is pressed with it empty, never on first render. Criteria are an `AttributeEditor` in grouped mode: AND groups of variable, operator and argument rows joined by OR, the variable a `Combobox` of the phase's variables, with Add condition, Add OR group, limits and announcements from the editor, and conditions and groups that reorder by grip, Move up and Move down, or Alt+Arrow keys (`reorderable`); behaviors are a second `AttributeEditor` (list mode, `reorderable`, up to 10) labelled Then, whose argument cell follows the behavior picked from a searchable list filtered by phase; Add behavior waits while the last behavior ends the rule. Every form resets when the drawer opens, so its content stays in place while it closes. A resource’s Rules tab opens it as Add Rule or Edit Rule. A save that fails keeps the drawer open with a danger `Alert`. Built from `SettingsSection`, `SettingsRow`, `Drawer` and its parts, `PanelHeader`, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `Field`, `Input`, `FieldDescription`, `Select`, `AttributeEditor`, `Combobox`, `RadioGroup` choice cards (`variant="card"`), `Card`, `Item`, `Switch`, `Alert` and `Button`.
edit/rule-builder.guidelinesSummary: A drawer where the user writes one rule of a rules engine: when it runs (the phase), the conditions that decide whether it applies, and the ordered behaviors it performs when they match. The user composes groups of variable, operator and argument rows (every row in a group must match, any group is enough), picks behaviors that fit the phase, puts everything in order and saves, without leaving the resource's Rules tab.

edit/schema-editor.name: SchemaEditor
edit/schema-editor.title: Blocks/Edit/SchemaEditor
edit/schema-editor.summary: The schema editing surface of a SQL database table, taken from the design sample's SQL database pages and the Console Kit's alter column and truncate dialogs: a flush `Card` holding the table's definition as a `DataTable` (column, type `Tag`, constraints, a Change type row menu) under a toolbar with the table name, its row count, Add column, the primary Insert row and a Table actions menu (Create Table, Truncate table). Create Table is a large right `Drawer` with the table Name and an `AttributeEditor` of column rows (reorderable by grip, Move up and down or Alt+Arrow; name, type `Select` with a search field and the type's glyph, default value, Primary `Checkbox`), validated on submit for an empty or malformed name, duplicate column names and no named column; the server's name conflict comes back as a danger `Alert` in the General section and on the field, per the form-validation rule. Add column is a large drawer with Name, Type, Default value and Primary key and Not null `Switch`es (a primary key forces Not null). Insert row is a large drawer with one `Field` per column, the auto-generated key disabled and NOT NULL columns required. Change type is a `ConfirmDialog` that warns the table is rebuilt and shows the statements that will run in a read-only `CodeEditor`; Truncate table is a `ConfirmDialog` with the statement and the typed table name. Every change runs async and ends in a toast whose actions fit the table (Insert row, Add column, Change again, Insert another), never a deploy action. The Create Table drawer also imports a CSV (`FileDropzone`, `FileTokenGroup` token, columns from the header with guessed types, a five-row preview) and adds foreign keys in a second `AttributeEditor` (column, referenced table and column, On delete). A page body for ConsoleLayout.
edit/schema-editor.guidelinesSummary: The table schema of a SQL database: the definition of one table and the drawers and dialogs that change it. A developer creates a table with its columns, adds a column, inserts a row by hand, changes a column's type or empties a table, and stays on the same surface while each change runs. It sits behind the Create Table, Add column, Insert and table menu buttons of `view/query-editor`. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header, the ⌘K palette and the `main`.

edit/variables.name: Variables
edit/variables.title: Blocks/Edit/Variables
edit/variables.summary: A key/value editor, drawn as a variables list page and the Create Variable drawer its heading action opens. The list follows the table-view recipe: one client-mode `useCollection` drives a `PropertyFilter`, `CollectionPreferences` and a data-driven `DataTable`, with a first-use and a no-match `EmptyState`; each row's Edit opens the drawer on that variable, Clone inserts a copy below it, and Delete opens the typed `ConfirmDialog` of delete-dialog. In the drawer the variables are an `AttributeEditor` (add, remove, focus, announcements, minimum one row) whose `row` slot draws each variable as a pair of `InputGroupRoot` rows with `InputGroupInput` fields, a Key row with a Remove button and a Value row with a show-value button and a Secret checkbox, beside a Form or JSON view and an Upload of a .env file; every scope is an `InputGroupRoot` joining its label, a `MultiSelect` of resources and an enable `Switch`, with Global giving way to any specific scope. Required and invalid states appear only after Save is pressed; every create, edit, clone and delete raises a success toast, and a save that fails keeps the drawer open with a danger `Alert`. Built from `AttributeEditor`, `PageHeader`, `PropertyFilter`, `CollectionPreferences`, `SettingsSection`, `DataTable`, `Card`, `EmptyState`, `TableCellId`, `TableCellLink`, `TableCellActions`, `Avatar`, `DropdownMenu`, `ConfirmDialog`, `Alert`, `Input`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `Drawer` and its parts, `PanelHeader`, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `InputGroupRoot`, `InputGroupAddon`, `InputGroupInput`, `Checkbox`, `ToggleGroup`, `MultiSelect`, `Switch`, `FieldError` and `Button`; the JSON view is a webkit `Textarea`. A page body for ConsoleLayout.
edit/variables.guidelinesSummary: A list of key and value pairs and the drawer that edits them, here environment variables. The user scans the variables already defined, then opens Create Variable to type or paste several pairs at once, mark the sensitive ones as secret, and select where they apply (the whole account, or specific environments, projects, services or policies) before saving them in one step. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header, the ⌘K palette and the `main`.

settings/settings-form.name: SettingsForm
settings/settings-form.title: Blocks/Settings/SettingsForm
settings/settings-form.summary: A settings form and its save strategy, one variant per strategy. SaveAll, the default (a form that is one logical unit has one save): account-level settings as `Item` rows saved as one unit, a page body for ConsoleLayout (the layout owns the shell and the main landmark): the form column opening with a small page heading, topic sections each a `SectionHeader` (an h2) over a flush `Card` of rows, and one full-bleed sticky footer with Discard and Save, both disabled until the form differs from what was saved (dirty tracking through `useUnsavedChanges`); a successful save confirms with a `Profile saved.` toast and a rejected one shows an error toast with Retry, the entries kept (SaveError); Profile is the example, with General (Full name, Email), Preferences (Timezone, Language) and Notifications (Product updates), and Full name and Email flag only after Save is pressed. SavePerGroup splits the page into topic groups whose `Card` footers each carry a secondary Save for that group only. SavePerCard splits a long configuration page into titled cards, each with an info `Alert`, its stacked fields and its own Save beside an optional docs `Link`. Profile is the full profile page of a signed-in account, and the layout every account settings page follows: seven `SettingsSection`s of flush `Card`s of rows with the unsaved-changes `SaveBar`, MFA linked to `account/mfa-settings`, and Delete account behind a type-to-confirm `ConfirmDialog`; ProfileLoading and ProfileError are its first load and its load failure. Saving one group or card disables just its own fieldset; the others stay editable, and each save confirms with a toast. Built from `PageHeader`, `SectionHeader`, `SettingsSection`, `SettingsRow`, `SaveBar`, `Card`, `Item`, `Alert`, `Field`, `Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Switch`, `Tag`, `Link`, `FieldError`, `ConfirmDialog`, `Skeleton` and `Button`.
settings/settings-form.guidelinesSummary: The place the user goes to change how an account or a project behaves. They scan a few topics, change one or two values, and commit them knowing exactly what the save covers. The block is one layout with three save strategies: one save for a form that is one logical unit, one save per group, or one save per card on a long configuration page. The Profile variant is the full account profile page, the layout every account settings page (billing details, credentials, users, teams) follows. The save model follows how the page is partitioned, not the container. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header, the breadcrumbs, the ⌘K palette and the `<main>`.

shell/console.name: Console
shell/console.title: Blocks/Shell/Console
shell/console.summary: The console shell as one component: `ConsoleLayout`, composed once in the app around RouterView, so a console page is only its body. Its `navigation` is the Azion console tree as data (Overview, Workloads, Deployments; Build, Secure, Store, Observe; Marketplace and the Settings drill-in), each row with an `href` the layout follows with the app's router, and the active row follows the route; it renders the resizable, collapsible rail with the wordmark and the account at its foot, the header with breadcrumbs, the search trigger, the app's actions and the avatar, the ⌘K palette listing every navigation page, and the single main. Below 768 px of its own width the rail becomes a drawer opened from the header's menu button. This block fills the slots: Create (`Button`) and Agent (`HighlightButton`), icon-only (`IconButton` with a `Tooltip`) while compact; Recents and Actions as `Command` groups; the account menu (`DropdownMenu` with `ThemeSwitcher`, Upgrade to Pro and `StatusIndicator`). The body is a stand-in list page (`PageHeader` and a `Card`) for view/table-view, which owns the controls row and the table; a page opens the same palette with useConsoleLayout().openSearch().
shell/console.guidelinesSummary: The application shell every signed-in page renders inside. The user browses and moves laterally between modules, so the shell keeps the whole product one step away: the navigation rail (wordmark, grouped navigation with drill-in levels, the account at its foot), one global header (breadcrumbs, search, the app's actions, the avatar) and the ⌘K palette. All of that is one component, `ConsoleLayout`: this block is the app's `App.vue` — compose it once around `RouterView` and every console page is only the body rendered through its default slot. The body here is a stand-in for `view/table-view`.

shell/docs.name: Docs
shell/docs.title: Blocks/Shell/Docs
shell/docs.summary: The documentation shell is `DocLayout`, composed once around the app's router view: this block's primary is the app's `App.vue` and every variant is a page body (an `<article>` only, with no header, rail, outline or footer of its own) that renders inside it. The layout owns the chrome and the DOCUMENT scrolls: a sticky docs header (the Azion Docs mark, the section links from `sections`, the search field that opens the ⌘K palette of every navigation page, and the `actions` slot with the GitHub `IconButton` and the Console `Button`), a sticky navigation rail from `lg` built from the `navigation` data (groups of rows with in-app `href`s followed with the router, inline subsections as `children`, the current row following the route) with the `ThemeSwitcher` in its `navigation-footer` slot and a drawer opened from the header below `lg`, the page in the layout's single main landmark, the sticky On this page rail from `xl` filled by the page itself (every `DocHeading` with an `anchor` at level 2 or 3 registers with the layout, in document order, and is tracked as the reader scrolls), the GitHub and Community `outline-groups` and a `DocCallToAction` in its `aside` slot (both shown only on pages with an outline), and the `Footer` (`variant="content"`) in the `footer` slot under the article, between the two rails; the primary's footer carries the columns, social links, status and language, with the brand leading the social row from `lg` (signature `compact`) and moving to the signature band below it, in CSS. No page wraps its article in a scroll area, a full-height frame or a layout of its own. The primary's stand-in page, in its default slot, is a short guide (`DocPageHeader`, then `DocProse` with anchored `DocHeading` sections); replace it with `<RouterView />`. Five variants are page bodies built from the documentation parts only: Article is a tutorial (First deploy) with breadcrumb, last updated and meta actions, a `DocCardGroup` chooser of paths, `DocCallout` tips, `DocSteps` with `CodeBlock` commands, a `DocPrompt`, Next steps, Related resources as `DocItem` rows in a `RegistrationFrame`, and `DocPreviousNext`; Reference is a product reference page (an info callout, two actions, the request path as a `Diagram` in a `DocFrame`, a JSON `CodeBlock`, a term list); Landing is the documentation home, whose headings carry no anchor so no outline rail shows: a `DocHero` with `Get started` and the `CopyPromptButton`, a `DocAgentCard` above the Console, CLI and API `DocCard`s, objectives, ready-made templates in their brand colours, Stop attacks, compliance, Follow along and the pager forward; AgentSetup is the index of agent setup pages: a `DocTabs` picker filtering `DocCard`s of coding agents by workflow, a comparison `DataTable` with check marks and `Tag`s, a legend `DocCallout` and a glossary of `DocCard` grids; AgentGuide is one agent's setup page: a masthead with the agent mark, fact `Tag`s and links, `DocSteps` with `DocCodeGroup` commands and `DocMarkdown` bodies, the MCP tools `DataTable`, CLI and context-file code, `DocItem` rows, `DocPrompt`s, tip callouts, FAQ and troubleshooting `DocAccordionGroup`s and the other agents grid.
