shell/docs.guidelinesSummary: The documentation shell. A reader comes to learn one task and leave, so the shell keeps the page readable and the next page close. It is `DocLayout`, composed once in the app around `RouterView`: the layout owns the docs header, the navigation rail, the "On this page" rail, the search palette and the footer, and the document itself scrolls with the header and both rails sticky. This block's primary is that `App.vue`; every variant is a page body, only its `<article>`, rendered in the layout's default slot. A page feeds the outline by rendering its section headings as anchored `DocHeading`s: each one registers with the layout, so the app passes nothing per page.

shell/site.name: Site
shell/site.title: Blocks/Shell/Site
shell/site.summary: The website shell: `SiteLayout` composed once in the app around RouterView, so the chrome is never rebuilt per page. The navigation is the SiteHeaderSection data (the azion.com mega-menus, Pricing, Contact, Login and Start for free, every item with its `href`) in `navigation`, and the footer is the SiteFooterSection data (`variant: 'site'`, columns, socials, status line, languages) in `footer`; the layout paints the canvas, owns the single `<main>`, and opens a ⌘K / Ctrl K Command palette that lists every navigation destination. Every page is only its sections in the default slot: one `Hero` band opening the page, then every section stacked inside one framed `SectionContainer max-width="site"` separated by hatched `SectionGap`s, ending on a closing frame that draws no rule of its own, so the SiteFooterSection closes the page frame. The hero, the sections and the footer all resolve to the site measure, which is the only reason the side rules running down the page are continuous. Built from `SiteLayout`, `Hero`, `Button`, `SectionContainer`, `SectionGap`, `SectionModule`, `RegistrationFrame`, `Stats` and `Texture`. The full mega-menus and the navigation sheet are documented on Templates › Marketing › Shell › SiteHeaderSection.
shell/site.guidelinesSummary: The marketing shell: one continuous frame — the site bar, a hero band that states the offer and the two next steps, every section stacked inside one framed container separated by hatched gaps, and the site footer closing the frame. The chrome is `SiteLayout`, composed once in the app around `RouterView` with the `SiteHeaderSection` and `SiteFooterSection` data; each page is only its sections, in the layout's slot.

state/async-submit.name: AsyncSubmit
state/async-submit.title: Blocks/State/AsyncSubmit
state/async-submit.summary: The async counterpart of the server rejection in the SectionRejected state of the FormValidation template: a deploy that runs for about half a minute, so the user walks away before it ends. The page heading carries the run status as a `Tag`: the page shows an `EmptyState` whose Deploy starts the run while idle, the deployment logs card while it runs, a danger `Alert` with Edit and Redeploy over the stopped logs when it fails, and a success `Alert` with Edit, Redeploy and Open service once it is live. Progress and the outcome also ride a toast wherever the user is: the app's one toast region (ToastPlugin, or one Toaster near the app root) shows it, never a Toaster in the page body; the Running frame shows the progress toast, and the failure (permanent) and success toasts carry Edit and Redeploy. Built from `PageHeader`, `Tag`, `Button`, `EmptyState`, `Alert`, and the deployment logs card of Templates/Platform/Detail/DeploymentLogs (`Card`, `StatusIndicator`, `LogViewer` with its `LogViewer.Steps` steps and progress bar, and `ToggleGroup` for the Phased or Complete log switch on failure). A page body: render it in the default slot of ConsoleLayout, which owns the rail, the header and the main.
state/async-submit.guidelinesSummary: The async-action pattern, and the standard for every build and deploy screen. A long-running action the user is free to walk away from: a deploy that runs for about half a minute and asks nothing while it does. The user's job is to start it, go on working anywhere in the console, and learn how it ended without coming back to check. The page that started the run shows its status in the heading, the logs while it runs and an inline outcome when it ends; in a full app the run lives outside the page, so its progress and its outcome also travel with the user as a toast, on success and on failure. This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`. The run toast rides the app's one toast region, never the page's: the app installs `ToastPlugin` (`app.use(ToastPlugin, { position: 'bottom-end' })`) or mounts one `Toaster` near its root, beside `ConsoleLayout`, and this page body only imports `toast` from `@aziontech/webkit/toast`. A `Toaster` inside a page body is a second region for the whole app: only the first `Toaster` to mount is active, and it gives that up when it unmounts, so a page's copy is either inert or, when it mounted first, stops every toast once the user leaves the page, the opposite of a run toast that follows the user. The docs preview mounts one region around the block the way an app root does, so its frames show the toasts; a copy of the page shows them wherever the app has mounted the region. The toasts are raised through `toast` with one id per run so each state replaces the last. Every outcome toast passes `actions: [{ label: 'Edit', onClick }, { label: 'Redeploy', onClick }]` and `closable: true`, so the app's `Toaster` renders both as `Toast.Action`s beside `Toast.Close`; the progress toast carries no action. The Running frame raises the progress toast, Error the permanent failure toast and Success the success toast; leaving the page dismisses the toast so the next story starts clean.

state/error-page.name: ErrorPage
state/error-page.title: Blocks/State/ErrorPage
state/error-page.summary: The page an app renders when it cannot show the address the user asked for. The primary is the 404: the content region centring an EmptyState whose figure is the animated azion-404 line figure (a still frame under reduced motion), the title Page not found, one sentence that says the address leads nowhere, and two actions, Go to home (primary) and Docs (outlined, new tab). A visually hidden h1 names the error code the figure shows. Variants cover 403 (no access, with Switch account), 500 (a failure on the server, with Retry, System status and an error reference for support) and a resource that does not exist inside the console (bordered EmptyState in the content column with Back to the list). Built from `EmptyState`, `Button`, `LineFigure` (azion-404) and the `svg/error-403` figure. A page body: render it in the default slot of ConsoleLayout, which owns the rail, the header and the main.
state/error-page.guidelinesSummary: The page an app renders when it cannot show the address the user asked for: the address leads nowhere (404), the user may not see it (403), or the server failed to build it (500). The user's job is to understand, in one sentence, that the problem is the address or the access and not their work, and to get somewhere useful in one click. The block keeps the error code out of the headline (it is in the figure and in a hidden `h1`) and says what happened in plain words. This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

state/first-use.name: FirstUse
state/first-use.title: Blocks/State/FirstUse
state/first-use.summary: The block a first-level list renders before the account owns any resource of that kind: a flush Card holding an EmptyState (the resource glyph, headline, lead and a Documentation link) over an Item.List of the ways to create the first one, each led by `Item.Media type="icon"` (the CLI method copies `azion deploy`), with the promo cards below it, each a link covering its card: Catalog templates (only for resource kinds that have a template catalog) and agent onboarding, whose frames carry the Claude, Codex, Gemini and Cursor marks from the webkit assets. The EmptyState’s icon slot shows the resource glyph; an app may draw a richer figure there. Every list that is still empty renders it with its own nouns, methods and promos. Built from Card, EmptyState, Item, Button, InputGroup, Input, CopyButton and Link. A page body: render it in the default slot of ConsoleLayout, which owns the rail, the header and the main.
state/first-use.guidelinesSummary: What a first-level list shows before the account owns any resource of that kind. The user's job is to create the first one, so the block replaces the empty table with a short explanation and every way to get started on the same screen: the methods to create one (import, CLI, from scratch), then the promotions that shortcut it (a Catalog template, a coding agent). Every list that is still empty renders this block with its own nouns, methods and promos. This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

state/form-validation.name: FormValidation
state/form-validation.title: Blocks/State/FormValidation
state/form-validation.summary: A standalone form that walks through every state a submit can land in, one story per state, on a single Create Variable page with no card around it: a heading, then `Field`s wrapping `Input`, `Select` and `Textarea` straight on the canvas in the form column, with Cancel and Create at the end of the column. Validation runs only on submit. An empty field takes the `required` state, a filled but wrong one takes `invalid`, and its helper text swaps the guidance for the message, so each field speaks in one place and there is no summary. Submit moves focus to the first field in error. A rejected request that no field owns raises an error toast with Retry and keeps the entries. A rejection a field owns, a key already in use, lands on that field and in a danger `Alert` above the fields, and never toasts. A successful save raises a success toast and clears the form. Its toasts go through `toast` into the app's one toast region (ToastPlugin, or one Toaster at the app root), never a Toaster in the page body. While the form loads, `Skeleton` rows stand in for the fields and Create is disabled. The block fetches nothing: Create emits `submit` with the values, and the page passes back `submitting`, `error`, `takenKey` or `saved`. Below md the actions stack at full width. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`; the Section variants add `SectionHeader`, `SettingsRow`, `SaveBar`, `AppHeader`, `Breadcrumb`, `Card`, `Item`, `MultiSelect`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`, `NumberInput` and `Alert`. The Section variants move the same rules to a long sectioned Create Service page (the creation header, section headings over flush `Card` groups of `Item` rows, a sticky `SaveBar`): another user deleted the linked origin, Save comes back with an error the Origin section owns, the page scrolls there, one danger `Alert` under the heading says what happened with the recovery action on it (Reload origins), and the Origin select turns invalid with its own reason and takes the focus; reloading swaps the select for a `Skeleton` and disables Save, and once reloaded the Alert closes and the select is flagged required. Never a toast, never a summary. A page body for a create page: render it under the focused creation header (top-bar/creation-bar), not in ConsoleLayout.
state/form-validation.guidelinesSummary: Every state a submit can land in, on one create form. The user's job is to create a resource and, when something stops the save, to know exactly which control to touch and that nothing they typed was lost. The primary is a short Create Variable page (heading, four fields straight on the canvas, Cancel and Create); the variants walk it through validation, the in-flight lock, an unscoped failure, a conflict, success and loading. The Section variants carry the same rules to a long sectioned create page, where the server rejects the save because of one section: another user deleted the origin the form links to, so the page takes the user to that section, says what happened and that nothing else was lost, offers the one action that recovers (Reload origins) and marks the field with its own reason. The Section variants are a focused create page with their own creation header and no rail. This block is a page body for a create page: render it under the focused creation header (`top-bar/creation-bar`), not in `ConsoleLayout`.

state/page-skeleton.name: PageSkeleton
state/page-skeleton.title: Blocks/State/PageSkeleton
state/page-skeleton.summary: The skeleton wires an app paints while a page is still arriving: the Home overview (Overview), the first-access Home (Onboarding), the whole shell while an expired session signs out (Session, with one body per family of page it covers: Session for a list, SessionDetail, SessionForm and SessionHome), and the version page (VersionDetail), sectioned cards whose rows end in a switch band. Each one is the real page’s grid drawn with Skeleton bands inside the same Card frames, so nothing shifts when the content lands. In the app the session wire is a fixed full-viewport layer sized to the measured header and rail; here it fills the canvas at the header’s 56px and the rail’s `--container-2xs`. Built from Skeleton, Card and Item; layout differences between rows switch on `data-*` attributes, never on a class ternary. Overview, Onboarding and VersionDetail are page bodies for the default slot of ConsoleLayout; the Session wires stand in for the whole app, layout included.
state/page-skeleton.guidelinesSummary: The skeleton wires an app paints while a page is still arriving. The user's job does not change while they wait: they need to see the shape of the page they asked for, so the wire draws the real page's grid with `Skeleton` bands inside the same `Card` frames, and nothing shifts when the content lands. The set covers the Home overview, the first-access Home, and the whole shell while an expired session signs out, drawn over the family of page it covers (list, detail, create form or Home). Overview and Onboarding are page bodies for the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`); the Session wires stand in for the whole app, layout included.

state/project-intake.name: ProjectIntake
state/project-intake.title: Blocks/State/ProjectIntake
state/project-intake.summary: The surfaces a project passes through when it is dropped on the page: the drop target (`FileDropzone` with `directories`, its title saying what dropping does and a Choose a folder `Button` as the keyboard way in), then the full-screen Initializing overlay: an `UploadProgress` card in the flow listing the received files with their status in words (Done, the percentage while uploading, Waiting), Cancel and Retry, over the upload summary. A large drop lists only the files still moving (at most 50 rows) while the heading keeps the counts. UploadError shows a file that failed: its row carries the reason and Retry, and a danger `Alert` above sums it up with Retry. A home page, its empty state, a creation hub and a project detail page render the drop target (the project page swaps the copy for “We build a new version of web-app, then you choose where it goes live.”); the home page, its empty state and the creation hub render Initializing over themselves. DropZone is a page body inside the default slot of ConsoleLayout; Initializing covers the whole screen.
state/project-intake.guidelinesSummary: The surfaces a project passes through when the user drops it on the page. The user's job is to deploy a folder they already have without filling in a form: a drop target fills the page body and says what will happen, with a Choose a folder button for anyone not dragging; once it is dropped, a full-screen Initializing overlay lists the received files with their status until the upload is done and the deploy takes over. DropZone is a page-body overlay inside the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`); Initializing covers the whole screen.

top-bar/auth-bar.name: AuthBar
top-bar/auth-bar.title: Blocks/TopBar/AuthBar
top-bar/auth-bar.summary: The console bar for the signed-out and onboarding screens: sign in, sign up, password recovery and the first-run steps. A `AppHeader` in its default `content` placement with the brand at the start and one outlined Documentation button at the end. There is no navigation, no search and no account control, because there is no session to act on yet. Built from `AppHeader`, `Button` and `Brand`.
top-bar/auth-bar.guidelinesSummary: The top bar of every signed-out and first-run screen: sign in, sign up, password recovery and the onboarding steps. The user has no session yet, so the bar has one job: say where they are (Azion) and offer the one way out that needs no account, the documentation. Everything a signed-in bar carries (navigation, search, Create, the account avatar) is left out because there is nothing to act on.

top-bar/creation-bar.name: CreationBar
top-bar/creation-bar.title: Blocks/TopBar/CreationBar
top-bar/creation-bar.summary: The console bar for the focused creation shell: create, edit and deploy flows that run without the navigation rail. A `AppHeader` in its default `content` placement, spanning the whole window. Start: a small back link with a `Tooltip`, the brand and the breadcrumb of where the flow lives. End: the account avatar alone, opening the account `DropdownMenu`, so the signed-in user stays visible. The bar carries no search, Create or Agent: the flow is the one thing on screen. Every one-screen create page (SinglePageCreate), every stepped one (MultipageCreate, with its CreateAndDeploy wizard), the deploy flows (DeployTemplate) and the CreateHub render it. The back button returns to the list the flow started from; a wizard drops it and the crumb once they reach the provisioning and success screens. Built from `AppHeader`, `Breadcrumb`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `Avatar`, `DropdownMenu` and `Brand`.
top-bar/creation-bar.guidelinesSummary: The top bar of the focused creation shell: create, edit and deploy flows that run without the navigation rail. The user is doing one task with a start and an end, so the bar gives them a linear way out (the back button and the breadcrumb to the list the flow started from) and keeps their identity visible (the avatar), and nothing else. No search, no Create, no Agent: the flow is the only thing on screen.

view/card-view.name: CardView
view/card-view.title: Blocks/View/CardView
view/card-view.summary: The card form of a first-level list page, for resources people recognise by a few fields rather than compare column by column: a medium page heading with the resource name and its one-line description and the outlined medium Documentation action beside a primary large Create Application, the page's only large control, then the controls row: a `PropertyFilter` (Name, Status, Region, Requests in 24h, or free text) that grows to fill the row, a Delete button that counts the selected cards and opens a `ConfirmDialog` (the delete-dialog pattern: a warning `Alert`, the selected names and an `Input` that must read delete), and `CollectionPreferences` for the page size and which fields every card shows; then `CardList` and a `Pagination`. Each card is named by a `Link` to the resource and lists its fields as label and value pairs (the status as a `Tag`, the domain isolated in `bdi`, the request count in compact notation). Four cards a row in a wide container, down to one in a narrow one (container queries). A visible Select all items sits above the cards and the selection survives paging. All of it runs on `useCollection` in client mode: the filter and the page live in the URL, and the page size and the visible fields are saved per account in localStorage. An account with no applications keeps the heading and the controls and shows a flush `Card` holding a medium `EmptyState` with a Create action; a load failure shows a danger `Alert` with Retry; a filter that matches nothing shows a No matching applications state with Clear filters. Laid out with the theme’s `layout-boundary`, `layout-column` and `layout-section-start` utilities. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`. A page body: render it in the default slot of ConsoleLayout, which owns the rail, the header and the main.
view/card-view.guidelinesSummary: The first-level index of one resource type, in cards. The user lands here from the sidebar to find a resource they recognise by its name and a few fields (its status, domain, region, traffic), narrow the list by those fields, open one, or select several and act on them together. One `useCollection` call holds the filter, the sort, the page, the selection across pages and the saved preferences, so the page is one heading over one band: the controls row, the cards and the pagination. This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

view/events-explorer.name: EventsExplorer
view/events-explorer.title: Blocks/View/EventsExplorer
view/events-explorer.summary: The events explorer (the app marks its Events navigation entry active): the controls row (`FilterMenu`, event search, Refresh and Download CSV) over the applied `FilterMenu.ChipGroup`, and the explorer. The explorer pairs a resizable, collapsible fields `Sidebar` (each field a column checkbox and a popover of its top values, grouped in an `Accordion` by category) with the log: the Events, Errors and Avg request time summary, the stacked volume chart whose buckets filter the period on click or drag, and the event `DataTable`. Each row's detail `IconButton` (or a row click) opens the event document beside the log in the end pane of a `Resizable` when the explorer is wide enough, and in a `Drawer` when it is not. A page body: render it in the default slot of ConsoleLayout, which owns the rail, the header and the main. Its root carries data-layout-fill, so the main stops scrolling and the fields panel, the log and the document scroll on their own.
view/events-explorer.guidelinesSummary: The events explorer. The user comes here to answer what happened on their traffic: how many events, how many errors, when they spiked, and what one event looked like in full. They narrow the log by fields and time, scan the rows, and open one event beside the log without losing their place. The fields, the log and the event document are three panes of one workspace, and every filter acts on all of them at once. This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`. The explorer is a workspace: its root carries `data-layout-fill`, so the layout's `main` stops scrolling, the root fills it, and the fields panel, the log and the event document each scroll on their own at every width (`h-dvh` only sizes a standalone preview).

view/file-browser.name: FileBrowser
view/file-browser.title: Blocks/View/FileBrowser
view/file-browser.summary: The file browser a storage resource opens on: one flush `Card` holding a borderless `DataTable` whose toolbar is the whole page header. The toolbar stacks the storage name beside the storage glyph, a large row of the table’s own search plus the refresh and download IconButtons and the `CollectionPreferences` (columns section), then a `Breadcrumb` of the folder path beside the Add to files `SplitButton` (Upload file, Add folder). Folders stay first under any sort with a link-coloured folder glyph and a link-button name that opens them, a .. row leads back up once inside a folder, Size sorts on bytes and Last modified on the timestamp, the rows page at 50, files take a glyph by extension, Size is muted and Last modified is `TableCellTime` (the editor's avatar and a relative time); folders carry Open and files Download in their row menu, with Delete below, which opens a `ConfirmDialog` (a warning `Alert` and an `Input` that must match the name). An empty folder renders the table’s empty slot: an `EmptyState` (This folder is empty) with a secondary Add to files split button, and a search that matches nothing shows No matching files with Clear search; inside a folder the .. row always remains. Built from `Card`, `DataTable` with `TableSearch`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `CollectionPreferences` (columns section), `Breadcrumb`, `SplitButton`, `TableCellTime`, `TableCellActions` and `EmptyState`. A page body: render it in the default slot of ConsoleLayout, which owns the rail, the header and the main.
view/file-browser.guidelinesSummary: The contents of one storage resource. The user opens a bucket to find a file, walk into a folder and back out, upload something or add a folder, and download or delete what is there. The table's toolbar is the whole page header, so the storage name, search, the folder path and Add to files all sit on the one surface the files live on. This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

view/marketplace.name: Marketplace
view/marketplace.title: Blocks/View/Marketplace
view/marketplace.summary: The marketplace page: a medium page heading with the outlined Documentation action over the integration catalog, the integrations installed into an existing application (templates live in `view/template-browser`): a Featured row of three `featured` `IntegrationCard`s (centred, raised, the context badge in the corner) while no filter is set, then All integrations: one `PropertyFilter` (free text over name, publisher and description; Publisher, Category, Context and Status as properties, all in the URL through `useCollection`) over a grid of `IntegrationCard` tiles with the logo, the name, by the publisher, two lines of description, the category badge, the Installed tag and an Install or Configure action. A tile opens the integration in a large right `Drawer`: name and publisher in the header, the description, `KeyValueList` (publisher, category, context, version, last update, the applications it runs on), an Overview in `DocProse`, the permissions it needs, and the install form, a required Application `Field` with a `Select` of the applications it is not on yet. Install is an async run (`state/async-submit`): the button shows `loading`, a progress toast follows the user, and the outcome lands as a toast and an inline `Alert` in the drawer; success carries Configure and Open application, failure is permanent and carries Edit and Reinstall. A search that matches nothing shows No matching integrations with Clear filters; while the catalog loads the tiles are skeletons. A page body: render it in the default slot of ConsoleLayout, which owns the rail, the header and the main.
view/marketplace.guidelinesSummary: The page where people find something made by Azion or a partner and add it to what they run. It lists integrations, installed into an existing application; templates, which start a new project, live in `view/template-browser`. People browse by need ("block bots", "split traffic"), compare by publisher and context, read what an integration does and what it may touch, then install it on one application and keep working while it installs. One `useCollection` call holds the search and the filters; one drawer holds the detail and the install; the install reports by toast wherever the person is. This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

view/query-editor.name: QueryEditor
view/query-editor.title: Blocks/View/QueryEditor
view/query-editor.summary: The query editor page (the app passes the Databases breadcrumb to the layout): the Tables and Editor tabs, each pairing a resizable, collapsible `Sidebar` (288px at rest) with a working pane. On Editor the panel holds the query history and the pane stacks the Run query, Prettify and Templates toolbar, the SQL `CodeEditor`, and the Results band (rows paged in a `DataTable`, or JSON in a copyable `CodeBlock`); on Tables the panel lists the tables as option `Item` rows and the pane holds the selected table with its Data and Definition switch, its rows in a paged, selectable `DataTable`. A database with no tables shows the Create Table empty state, and the Templates button opens the SQL quick templates drawer. Its page-level parts are `PageTabs`. A page body: render it in the default slot of ConsoleLayout, which owns the rail, the header and the main; CreateDatabase is a focused create page with its own header and no rail, rendered outside it. Its root carries data-layout-fill (every variant but CreateDatabase), so the main stops scrolling and the panel, the rows, the editor and the results scroll on their own.
view/query-editor.guidelinesSummary: The workspace of one SQL database. The user comes here to see which tables exist, read and edit a table's rows or its definition, and write and run queries against the data. Two tabs share one layout: a resizable side panel that lists things (tables, or past queries) beside a working pane that shows the one in use. This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`. The editor is a workspace: its root carries `data-layout-fill`, so the layout's `main` stops scrolling, the root fills it, and the side panel, the rows, the editor and the results each scroll on their own at every width (`h-dvh` only sizes a standalone preview). CreateDatabase is a focused create page with its own header and no rail, rendered outside it.

view/rule-list.name: RuleList
view/rule-list.title: Blocks/View/RuleList
view/rule-list.summary: An ordered list of rules grouped by phase, the Rules tab of an application or a firewall. A `PageHeader` with Documentation and Add Rule sits over a search `Input` and a flush `Card` holding an `Accordion` with one item per phase (Request, Response), each trigger reading the phase and its rule count and each panel a data-driven `DataTable` (scrolling sideways when narrow) with the grip, Position, Name, Description, Status and Last modified. The table is `reorderable`: its grip drags the row or moves it with the arrow keys, Home and End, and `row-reorderable` pins the locked rule; a Position cell adds a numeric position `Input` (type a position and press Enter to move the rule there; disabled with the lock reason on the locked rule) and Move up and Move down `IconButton`s; every move is announced in a polite status region and focus follows the moved rule. A leading locked rule (the default rule) keeps first place and cannot be turned off; a search turns reordering off and says so in an info `Alert`. The Status cell is a `Switch` that turns a rule on or off without losing its place. Any change raises a `SaveBar` with Discard and Review changes; Review changes opens a `Dialog` listing, per phase, every rule that moves (from and to) and every rule turned on or off, with Cancel and Save, and a danger `Alert` in the dialog when the save fails. A success toast confirms the saved order. Built from `PageHeader`, `Button`, `Input`, `Alert`, `Card`, `Accordion`, `DataTable`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `Tag`, `Switch`, `EmptyState`, `SaveBar`, `Dialog` and its parts, `PanelHeader`, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`; its toasts go through `toast` into the app's one toast region (ToastPlugin, or one Toaster at the app root), never a Toaster in the page body. A page body: render it in the default slot of ConsoleLayout, which owns the rail, the header and the main.
view/rule-list.guidelinesSummary: An ordered list of rules grouped by phase: the Rules tab of an application (Request and Response phases) or a firewall (Request only). Order is behavior here, so the list is built to change the order safely: drag, keys, a typed position or Move up and Move down move a rule, every move is announced, and nothing runs in the new order until the user reviews the changes and saves. This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

view/table-view.name: TableView
view/table-view.title: Blocks/View/TableView
view/table-view.summary: The canonical first-level list page: a medium page heading with the resource name and its one-line description, the outlined medium Documentation action and a primary large Create Resource, the page's only large control (on a phone they stack below the copy, each at full width), then the controls row and the resource table, laid out with the console page column and section rhythm. The whole list runs on `useCollection` in client mode: a `PropertyFilter` grows to fill the controls row and turns Name, Author, Status, Domain or free text into removable tokens (Match all or Match any, Clear filters, the match count), the sortable headers sort, the footer pages, and the filter, the sort and the page live in the URL so a filtered list can be shared. Beside the filter sit Refresh (the table’s loading state), Download CSV (every matching row) and `CollectionPreferences`, a dialog for the page size, the columns (shown, hidden and ordered; Name always shows), wrapped lines, striped rows and density, saved in localStorage. Any resource index takes this shape with its own columns and properties. The row menu's Delete opens a `ConfirmDialog` (the delete-dialog pattern: a warning `Alert` and an `Input` that must match the resource name). A filter that matches nothing shows a No matching resources `EmptyState` with Clear filters inside the table; when the account has no resources left, the page keeps its heading and the controls row, and the table, without its header and footer, gives way to a flush `Card` holding only a medium `EmptyState` (the resource glyph, then a small secondary Create Resource and a small outlined Documentation on one row), so the list survives its last row being deleted. Laid out with the theme’s `layout-boundary`, `layout-column` and `layout-section-start` utilities carrying the inset, the measure and the vertical rhythm. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`. A page body: render it in the default slot of ConsoleLayout, which owns the rail, the header and the main.
view/table-view.guidelinesSummary: The first-level index of one resource type, in rows. The user lands here from the sidebar to find a resource among many, narrow the list by its attributes, compare records column by column, and act on one: open it, deploy it, clone it, delete it, or create a new one. One `useCollection` call holds the filter, the sort, the page and the saved preferences, so the page is one heading over one band: the controls row and the table it narrows. This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

view/template-browser.name: TemplateBrowser
view/template-browser.title: Blocks/View/TemplateBrowser
view/template-browser.summary: The template catalog people start a project from: a medium page heading with the outlined Documentation action, one `PropertyFilter` that searches the name and the description and filters by Category and Framework, then one section per category (Frameworks, Starters, Functions) with a grid of template tiles. Each tile is an `IntegrationCard` with the framework mark, the name as a button that opens the preview, two lines of description and the framework as a badge; the whole tile is the target, and the grid follows the content width through container queries. The preview is a large right `Drawer`: the mark and the name in the header, the description, a `KeyValueList` of framework, category, repository and last update, and the template's README in a `Card` through `DocProse`; its footer holds View repository and the primary Deploy, which leads to the deploy template flow (`create/deploy-template`), where the deploy runs and reports by toast. The filter lives in the URL through `useCollection`. A search that matches nothing shows No matching templates with Clear filters; while the catalog loads the tiles are skeletons; a catalog that fails to load shows a danger `Alert` with Retry and an Import from Git way out. Built from `PageHeader`, `Button`, `PropertyFilter`, `Card`, `IntegrationCard`, `EmptyState`, `Drawer`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerTitle`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `KeyValueList` and `DocProse`. A page body: render it in the default slot of ConsoleLayout, which owns the rail, the header and the main.
intents: começar a partir de um template
view/template-browser.guidelinesSummary: The catalog of templates a person starts a project from. They arrive from the creation hub or a "Start from a template" link, already knowing roughly what they want (a framework, a kind of site, a small function) and needing to find it, check what it contains and start the deploy. The page is one heading over one band: a single search and filter control, then the templates grouped by category. A tile opens a preview drawer with the facts and the README, and the drawer's Deploy hands off to the deploy template flow, which owns the run and its outcome. This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

view/waf-tuning.name: WafTuning
view/waf-tuning.title: Blocks/View/WafTuning
view/waf-tuning.summary: The Tuning tab of a WAF rule set: the requests it matched, grouped by rule, so the user can allow the legitimate ones. A `PageHeader` with Export to CSV and an allow action that reads Allow selected, then Allow n selected once rows are checked; threshold settings above the table (a Time range `Select`, a Minimum hits `Input` that validates as a whole number, a search `Input` and a Refresh `IconButton`); and a flush `Card` with a data-driven `DataTable` with row selection and sorting (Rule ID, Threat, Hits sorted high to low, and the top IP addresses, countries and paths, as `TableCellTags` whose `+N` popover lists the rest). Rows below the minimum hits drop out, and a table with none left shows a small `EmptyState` saying how to widen it; a search that matches nothing shows No matching rules with Clear search, and a load failure shows a danger `Alert` with Retry. Allowing opens a `Dialog` form listing the selected rules and how many allowed rules will be created (one per rule and path), with a required Reason `Textarea` whose error shows only after Allow rules is pressed; success closes it, clears the selection and raises a success toast, failure keeps it open with a danger `Alert` and Try again. Built from `PageHeader`, `Button`, `Field`, `Select`, `Input`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `Card`, `DataTable`, `TableCellTags`, `EmptyState`, `Dialog` and its parts, `PanelHeader`, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `Alert`, `Textarea`; its toasts go through `toast` into the app's one toast region (ToastPlugin, or one Toaster at the app root), never a Toaster in the page body. A page body: render it in the default slot of ConsoleLayout, which owns the rail, the header and the main.
view/waf-tuning.guidelinesSummary: The Tuning tab of a WAF rule set. It shows the requests the rule set matched, grouped by the rule that matched them, with enough context (hits, top addresses, countries and paths) for the user to tell an attack from a false positive, and turns the legitimate ones into allowed rules with a recorded reason. This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.
